title: Israeli Strikes Kill 7 Across Gaza, Destroy Aid Warehouse Storing Malnutrition Supplies
detail: Overnight into Tuesday, August 25, 2026, Israeli strikes killed at least seven Palestinians across Gaza. A strike on a residential building in Deir al-Balah destroyed adjacent warehouses belonging to the Land of Man Association, burying nutritional supplements meant for malnourished children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers; Ard El Insan project coordinator Sahar Salem said 'losing these quantities in their entirety is a major blow to our work.' A separate strike hit a home in Beit Lahiya near Kamal Adwan Hospital, killing three Palestinians and wounding others. A drone strike on a gathering of civilians in Khan Younis's al-Mawasi area killed one man and wounded three more. Gaza Ministry of Health Director-General Dr. Munir al-Bursh said the strikes were the latest in ongoing violations of the October 2025 ceasefire; the Israeli military did not immediately comment on the individual strikes.

media.caption: A boy sits on the frame of a destroyed vehicle near the rubble of collapsed buildings in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, August 25, 2026

confidenceReason: Casualty figures corroborated by Gaza Ministry of Health, Al Jazeera correspondent reporting, and a Times of Israel liveblog entry citing Palestinian media reports; IDF has not disputed the strikes occurred but has not detailed individual targets.

title: Settlers Pepper-Spray and Beat Israeli Activists, AFP Journalist Near Bethlehem as Soldiers Watch
detail: On Tuesday, August 25, 2026, masked Israeli settlers attacked a group of left-wing Israeli activists from Rabbis for Human Rights and other rights organizations, along with French AFP journalists, at an outpost near the Palestinian village of Jannatah south of Bethlehem in the southern West Bank. The activists had traveled to help residents build a fence around homes that had come under repeated settler attack. Rabbis for Human Rights said the assailants pepper-sprayed activists, beat a 70-year-old participant, and smashed windows and slashed tires on four vehicles; the Palestine Red Crescent Society said five people were treated for injuries, and one AFP journalist suffered a bleeding chin after being struck with a stick. IDF soldiers were present throughout but made no arrests, with the military saying troops attempted to separate the groups 'with little success'; police arrived only hours after the assault had ended. The attack came amid a broader wave of West Bank settler violence documented by rights groups in recent weeks.

media.caption: Israeli settlers confront left-wing activists and AFP journalists near the village of Jannatah, south of Bethlehem, August 25, 2026

confidenceReason: Attack corroborated by Rabbis for Human Rights, the Palestine Red Crescent Society, and independent Times of Israel and Haaretz reporting citing AFP journalists present at the scene; IDF has not disputed that the attack occurred or that no arrests were made.

title: Israeli Forces Raid and Seize UNRWA Vocational Training Center in East Jerusalem; Guterres Condemns 'Unauthorized Incursion'
detail: On Tuesday, August 25, 2026, Israeli police and military forces raided the UNRWA-run Qalandiya Training Centre, located between the Kafr Aqab neighborhood and the Qalandiya refugee camp in occupied East Jerusalem, and forcibly expelled all UNRWA staff, telling them not to return. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir took part in the operation and said 'there is no place for the agency in Jerusalem and Israel.' Five Palestinians were injured during the raid. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel 'will not allow an organization whose employees were involved in terrorism and in the October 7 massacre to operate on its territory, and will take action against it using every means at its disposal.' UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the raid, with UN officials stating that UN premises are 'inviolable and immune from any form of interference'; UNRWA called it an 'unauthorised and deeply concerning incursion.' Israeli officials said the land had belonged to the Jewish National Fund since 1937 and announced plans to convert the facility, which trained roughly 340 Palestinians a year, into a municipal educational complex; human rights lawyer Mohammad Dahleh called the seizure a violation of international law citing the ICJ's December 2025 advisory opinion.

media.caption: Israeli forces at the UNRWA Qalandiya Training Centre in Kafr Aqab, East Jerusalem, August 25, 2026

confidenceReason: Raid and expulsion of staff confirmed directly by UNRWA and Netanyahu's own statement claiming responsibility, corroborated by Al Jazeera and Times of Israel reporting; UN Secretary-General's office condemnation independently confirms the incident.

title: Far-Right MK Zvi Sukkot Smashes Palestinian Memorial With Sledgehammer During IDF-Escorted West Bank Tour
detail: On Tuesday, August 25, 2026, Religious Zionism MK Zvi Sukkot took a sledgehammer to a stone memorial listing 10 Palestinians — including members of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine's armed wing — who died between 1930 and 2004, in the village of Madama south of Nablus in the northern West Bank, during a tour that had been coordinated with and escorted by the Israeli military. Sukkot posted video of the act, calling it a 'terror monument' and telling reporters it was 'a small taste' of what should follow. The IDF said Sukkot and his aides had acted 'deceptively and manipulatively,' stating that 'contrary to the coordination, the participants acted... in complete violation of the approved outline, and began demolishing one of the memorials'; the military said it regularly demolishes such memorials itself through authorized channels but criticized Sukkot for misusing the escorted tour rather than for the act of vandalism itself. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot both commented on the episode amid broader criticism of the government's handling of West Bank settler activity.

media.caption: MK Zvi Sukkot wields a sledgehammer against a Palestinian memorial in Madama, West Bank, August 25, 2026

confidenceReason: Confirmed by Sukkot's own video and public statements and by an IDF statement acknowledging the incident occurred during an authorized-but-misused tour; corroborated independently by ABC News and Times of Israel.
